rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse addressed Medinan Jews who urged Muslim relatives and in-laws to remain in their faith and follow the Prophet, though they did not practice that advice.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزلت هذه الآية في يهود أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports that Salman asked the Prophet about the worship and prayers of his former religious companions, and the verse beginning “Those who believe…” was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال قال سلمان سألت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أهل دين كنت معهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives another account: after Salman described his companions, the Prophet said they were in Hell; Salman was deeply distressed until the verse through “they shall not grieve” was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال لما قص سلمان على رسول الله قصة أصحابه قال هم في النار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about Salman al-Farisi’s companions.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال نزلت هذه الآية في أصحاب سلمان الفارسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jewish scholars and Christians from Najran disputed each other’s religions; each side rejected the other’s prophet and scripture, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لما قدم أهل نجران من النصارى على رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Abbas says Quraysh prevented the Prophet from praying at the Kaaba in the Sacred Mosque, occasioning the verse.
rows.anchor: أن قريشا منعوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عند الكعبة في المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: زيد
rows.claim: Zayd says the verse concerns the polytheists who barred the Messenger from entering Mecca at al-Hudaybiya.
rows.anchor: عن زيد قال نزلت في المشركين حين صدوا رسول الله عن مكة يوم الحديبية

rows.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة
rows.claim: A Bedouin asked whether God was near, so they could converse privately, or far, so they should call aloud; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن الصلت بن حكيم بن معاوية بن حيدة عن أبيه عن جدة قال جاء أعرابي إلى النبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet’s Companions asked where their Lord was, and this verse was revealed; al-Suyuti notes the report is mursal and has other routes.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال سأل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أين ربنا فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that after the Prophet urged people not to tire of supplication, a man asked whether God hears prayer; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تعجزوا عن الدعاء فإن الله أنزل علي

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says people wondered when to pray after 40:60 (“Call upon Me; I will answer you”), so 2:186 through “they may be rightly guided” was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح أنه بلغه لما نزلت ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that after a raid party including Asim and Mirthad was killed, two hypocrites disparaged them for dying instead of staying home or delivering the Prophet’s message; the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لما أصيبت السرية التي فيها عاصم ومرثد قال رجلان من المنافقين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq: he professed Islam to the Prophet, then burned Muslims’ crops and hamstrung their donkeys, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق أقبل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib reports that Suhayb offered his Meccan property to the Quraysh pursuers in return for being allowed to emigrate; the Prophet called it a profitable sale, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال أقبل صهيب مهاجرا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأتبعه نفر من قريش

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A mursal report from Ikrima gives a similar account of the verse’s revelation concerning Suhayb’s emigration bargain.
rows.anchor: من مرسل عكرمة وأخرجه أيضا من طريق جاد بن سلمة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A report from Anas explicitly says the verse was revealed about this event; al-Hakim graded this version sound according to Muslim’s criteria.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت عن أنس وفيه التصريح بنزول الآية وقال صحيح على شرط مسلم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the verse also concerns Abu Dharr and Jundub ibn al-Sakan, one of Abu Dharr’s people, alongside Suhayb.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال نزلت في صهيب وأبي ذر وجندب ابن السكن أحد أهل أبي ذر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Companions feared the burden of 2:284; the Prophet taught them to say they heard and obeyed, after which 2:285 was revealed and 2:286 lifted the burden. Muslim also transmits a similar report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة لما نزلت ﴿ وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله ﴾ اشتد ذلك على الصحابة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In Abu Hurayra’s account, God abrogated the earlier burden by revealing “God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة لما نزلت ﴿ وإن تبدوا ما في أنفسكم أو تخفوه يحاسبكم به الله ﴾ اشتد ذلك على الصحابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Muslim and others transmit from Ibn Abbas an account similar to Abu Hurayra’s report about the revelation of these closing verses.
rows.anchor: وروى مسلم وغيره عن ابن عباس نحوه

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: Qatada ibn al-Numan reports that Banu Ubayriq stole his uncle’s food and weapons, blamed Labid, and accused Qatada and his uncle; revelation vindicated them and exposed the thieves. Al-Hakim graded the report sound on Muslim’s criteria.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ابن النعمان قال كان أهل بيت منا يقال لهم بنو أبيرق بشر وبشير ومبشر

rows.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
rows.claim: The same account says the Prophet returned the weapon to Rifa'a; Bashir fled to the polytheists, and the later warning about opposing the Messenger was revealed concerning him.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل القرآن أتى رسول الله عليه وسلم بالسلاح فرده إلى رفاعة ولحق بشير بالمشركين

rows.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
rows.claim: Mahmud ibn Labid says Bashir stole food and two suits of armor from Rifa'a’s loft, denied it, and blamed Labid; revelation exposed Bashir and cleared Labid.
rows.anchor: عن محمود بن لبيد قال عدا بشير ابن الحرث على علية رفاعة بن زيد عم قتادة بن النعمان

rows.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
rows.claim: Mahmud’s account says Bashir fled to Mecca as an apostate, attacked the Prophet and Muslims in verse, and was lampooned by Hassan ibn Thabit until he returned; this occurred in Rabi II, year four AH.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل القرآن في بشير وعثر عليه هرب إلى مكة مرتدا فنزل على سلامة بنت سعد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith claimed al-Lat and al-Uzza would intercede for him, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال قال النضر بن الحرث سوف تشفع إلى اللات والعزي فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Muslims cursed the unbelievers’ idols, so the unbelievers cursed God; the prohibition on insulting their invoked deities was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال كان المسلمون يسبون أصنام الكفار فيسب الكفار الله فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi reports that Quraysh demanded the Safa hill become gold; Gabriel offered either to grant it with punishment if they disbelieved or leave them time to repent, and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي قال كلم رسول الله قريشا فقالوا يا محمد تخبرنا أن موسى كان معه عصا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that a client of Banu Adi killed an Ansari and the Prophet fixed blood money at twelve thousand; the verse about their grievance was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أن مولى بني عدي بن كعب قتل رجلا من الأنصار فقضى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالدية اثني عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A weak report from Abu Umama says Thalaba promised charity if made wealthy, then expanded flocks led him to abandon congregational prayer; when collectors arrived he refused, and 9:75–77 was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن ثعلبة ابن حاطب قال يا رسول الله ادع الله أن يرزقني مالا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also transmits a version of the Thalaba story concerning the revelation of 9:75–77.
rows.anchor: من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس نحوه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the Prophet strained to memorize each recitation from Gabriel, fearing he would leave before the Prophet learned it; the command not to hasten the Quran was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن السدي قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بالقرآن أتعب نفسه في حفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti notes another cause had been given in Surat al-Nisa, but prefers al-Suddi’s account as more sound.
rows.anchor: وتقدم في سورة النساء سبب آخر وهذا أصح

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi reports that the Prophet sent him to a Jewish man to borrow flour until Rajab; when collateral was demanded, the Prophet affirmed his trustworthiness in heaven and earth, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود أن أسلفني دقيقا

rows.speaker: عدي بن ثابت
rows.claim: A woman of the Ansar asked how to protect her privacy when relatives entered her home while she was in a state she did not want them to see; the permission verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت جاءت إمرأة من الأنصار فقالت يا رسول الله إني أكون في بيتي على حال

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Abu Bakr asked how Quraysh merchants traveling between Mecca, Medina, and Syria could enter known roadside houses without residents; the verse exempting uninhabited houses followed.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حبان قال لما نزلت آية الاستئذان في البيوت قال أبو بكر يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says they used to call Zayd ibn Haritha “Zayd ibn Muhammad” until the command to call adopted sons by their fathers was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد جتى نزل في القرآن

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa recounts the terrifying darkness and wind during the Confederates’ siege; hypocrites claimed their homes were exposed and slipped away, then the Prophet sent him to scout. He found the wind scattering the enemy, and the reminder of God’s favor was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة قال لقد رأيتنا ليلة الأحزاب ونحن صافون قعودا وأبو سفيان ومن معه من الأحزاب فوقنا

rows.speaker: عمرو المزني
rows.claim: A report from the grandfather of Kathir ibn Abdullah says the Prophet struck a trench rock three times; each spark disclosed future conquests at Hira and Persian cities, Byzantine palaces, and Sana'a. Hypocrites mocked the promises while fearing the siege, prompting 33:12.
rows.anchor: من طريق كثير بن عبد الله ابن عمرو المزني عن أبيه عن جده قال خط رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الخندق

rows.speaker: ابن جويبر
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the hypocritical claim that God and His Messenger promised only delusion was uttered by Muattib ibn Qushayr al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جويبر عن ابن عباس قال نزلت هذه الآية في متعب بن قشير الأنصاري

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the backbiting verse was said to concern Salman al-Farisi: after he ate and fell asleep snoring, someone criticized his eating and sleep.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال زعموا أنها نزلت في سلمان الفارسي أكل ثم رقد فنفخ

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Mulayka reports that after Bilal called the prayer from atop the Kaaba at the conquest, people objected to a Black enslaved man doing so; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة قال لما كان يوم الفتح رقى بلال على ظهر الكعبة فأذن

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن أبي داود
rows.claim: A report found in Ibn Bishkuwal’s handwriting attributes the verse to Abu Hind: the Prophet urged Banu Bayada to marry him to one of their women, and they objected to giving their daughters to freedmen.
rows.anchor: وجدت بخط ابن بشكوال أن أبا بكر ابن أبي داود أخرج في تفسير له أنها نزلت في أبي هند

rows.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري
rows.claim: Thabit ibn al-Harith reports that Jews called a child who died young a “sidq”; the Prophet rejected this and said God knows whether each person formed in the womb will be wretched or fortunate.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال كانت اليهود تقول إذا هلك لهم صبي صغير هو صديق

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that during an expedition a man unable to find a mount asked a friend for help; the friend offered a ride in exchange for taking on his sins, and these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في غزوة فجاء رجل يريد أن يحمل فلم يجد ما يخرج عليه

rows.speaker: دراج أبو السميع
rows.claim: Darraj Abu al-Samih gives another expedition account: after the Prophet could not carry a man, another person offered a mount so he could catch the army with his good deeds; the passage through 53:41 was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن دراج أبي السميع قال خرجت سرية غازية فسأل رجل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يحمله

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says a convert’s former co-religionist offered to assume his sins if he paid; the convert gave money, was pressed for more, and signed a witnessed agreement, prompting the verses.
rows.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال ان رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال أتركت دين الأشياخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people used to pass the Prophet while he prayed with their heads held high; the verse “while you are samidun” was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كانوا يمرون على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي شامخين فنزلت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports seeing the moon split in two at Mecca before the Prophet’s migration; people called it magic, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال رأيت القمر منشقا شقتين بمكة قبل مخرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that Meccans asked the Prophet for a sign, whereupon the moon split twice at Mecca and the opening verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال سأل أهل مكة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية فانشق القمر بمكة مرتين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the polytheists declared on the day of Badr that they were united and victorious; the prophecy that the assembly would be routed was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالوا يوم بدر نحن جميع منتصر فنزلت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed with the Messenger about divine decree, prompting the passage from “the criminals are in error” through “We created everything according to a measure.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في القدر فنزلت

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says people called the Prophet mad and then a devil, prompting the assurance that he was not mad by his Lord’s favor.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال كانوا يقولون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه مجنون ثم شيطان فنزلت

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says no one had better character than the Prophet: whenever a Companion or family member called him, he answered, “At your service”; this occasioned the verse.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت ما كان أحد أحسن خلقا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما دعاه أحد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq as the person meant by the warning against obeying a habitual swearer; al-Kalbi gives the same identification.
rows.anchor: عن السدي في قوله ﴿ ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين ﴾ قال نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth as the person meant by the warning against the habitual swearer.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قال نزلت في الأسود بن عبد يغوث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the warning was revealed first, but they did not know whom it meant until “zanīm” was later revealed; they recognized the man by his sheep-like earlobe.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ ولا تطع كل حلاف مهين هماز مشاء بنميم ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Jahl ordered captives tied up rather than killed at Badr; the garden parable was revealed about their power over the captives, like the garden owners’ power over their garden.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج ان أبا جهل قال يوم بدر خذوهم أخذا فاربطوهم في الحبال ولا تقتلوا

rows.speaker: بريدة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet told Ali he was commanded to draw him near, teach him, and ensure he retained the teaching; the verse about a receptive ear was revealed. Al-Suyuti says the report is unsound.
rows.anchor: عن بريده قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لعلي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet neither recited to nor saw the jinn: a group heard his dawn prayer at Nakhla after heavenly news was blocked, then returned to announce wondrous Quran; only their words were revealed to him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الجن ولا رآهم ولكنه انطلق في طائفة من أصحابه

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Abd Allah recounts meeting an enormous jinn in an ancient stone city, praying toward the Kaaba in a wool cloak said to be 700 years old; the jinn attributed decay to sinful smells and unlawful food and claimed faith in Jesus and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن عبد الله قال كنت في ناحية ديار عاد إذ رأيت مدينة من حجر منقور وسطها قصر

rows.speaker: كردم بن أبي السائب الأنصاري
rows.claim: Kardam ibn Abi al-Saib reports that while he and his father slept near a shepherd, a wolf seized a lamb; the shepherd called on the valley’s jinn guardian, an unseen voice called the wolf, and the lamb returned. The verse about humans seeking jinn protection was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن كردم بن أبي السائب الأنصاري قال خرجت مع أبي إلى المدينة في حاجة وذلك أول ما ذكر رسول الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the promise of abundant water for those upright on the path concerned Quraysh unbelievers, who had endured seven years without rain.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل في قوله ﴿ وأن لو استقاموا على الطريقة لأسقيناهم ماء غدقا ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the jinn asked permission to attend prayers with the Prophet in his mosque, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت الجن يا رسول الله ائذن لنا أن نشهد معك الصلوات في مسجدك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr gives a similar report: the jinn asked how they could attend the mosque and prayer while far from the Prophet, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال قالت الجن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف لنا أن نأتي المسجد ونحن ناءون عنك

rows.speaker: حضرمي
rows.claim: Hadrami reports a jinn’s boast that it could protect Muhammad; the declaration that none can protect him from God was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: عن حضرمي أنه ذكر له أن جنيا من الجن من أشرافهم ذا تبع قال إنما يريد محمد أن يجيره الله
